evidence: Route 1, paper Table 1 (10.1371/journal.pone.0220930.t001), which publishes M, SD, %Min and %Max per item for all 18. Every live item reproduces its own published row: e.g. PSIS-Y-SF_01 4.21/0.917/2.3%/45.7% vs published 4.21/0.917/2.3/45.7; PSIS-Y-SF_13 4.51/0.856/1.0/69.1 vs 4.51/0.856/1.0/69.1; PSIS-Y-SF_18 2.12/0.987/29.3/3.0 vs 2.12/0.987/29.3/3.0. Largest deviation across all 18 items x 4 statistics is 0.005 (PSIS-Y-SF_11 mean 2.62 live vs 2.63 printed, rounding). Uniqueness was tested, not just agreement: each of the 18 published rows is nearest to its OWN live item, minimum margin to the runner-up 0.181 (row 7), so every item is distinguished from every other -- including the near-tied mean pairs rows 5/10 (2.94 vs 2.95, separated by %Min/%Max 5.9/5.6 vs 14.1/8.9) and rows 7/16 (both 2.45, separated by 22.0/6.9 vs 16.4/5.6). What this does NOT establish: the response-option anchor labels, which no statistic can test and on which the paper contradicts itself (Methods 'almost never'..'almost always' vs Table 1 footnote 'strongly disagree'..'strongly agree'); the shipped labels are the Table 1 footnote's, disclosed in public_note.
